identity.real_world_identity_notes: Mid-engined racing version of the M1 built for the one-make Procar series that supported Formula One in 1979 and 1980. It keeps the road car's ZF five-speed, whose first gear sits on a dogleg so that first, third and fifth share the lower plane, with revised ratios and an added oil cooler for racing.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
There is no automation: the clutch is needed to pull away, the driver lifts the throttle to upshift and blips it to downshift.

The dogleg gate was seen directly in the cockpit during the guided drive and is independently corroborated by the registered sources. First gear sits out of the racing shift plane, so second through fifth fall in one straight sequence.

The gearbox construction stays unestablished after reading the car's FIA forms, and the reason is worth keeping. The Group 4 form contemporary with the Procar predates the article 603 layout: it has no synchroniser field, so it is silent rather than negative, and an absent field must not be read as a no.

The later Group B form does mark both its five-speeds synchronised, and they are recognisably the same ZF unit by their ratios. That is suggestive and it is not enough: it postdates the Procar by three years, the Procar has no form of its own, and the one earlier ratio set that appears nowhere else was struck through on the transfer. No M1 five-speed is shown as dog-engaged on any form, so nothing here argues for a dog box either.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.bmw-m1-procar.20260813t202518185z-ae57bdec by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: Registered sources establish the real-world identity and transmission, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The sources establish a ZF five-speed with a dogleg first gear, and the live drive confirmed five gears through an H-pattern gate observed as a dogleg. The guided drive observed the gate in the cockpit and reported an ordinary dogleg, with first down and to the left of the racing plane. The gate is corroborated by a primary source: section 603 f) of the M1's Group B homologation form draws reverse above first with 1, 3 and 5 on the lower plane.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
The guided drive recorded that the upshift was accepted after a throttle lift and the downshift after the driver's manual blip, with no automatic cut or blip detected.

driver_summary: The road car's ZF five-speed with a dogleg gate - first is down and left, outside the racing plane, so second through fifth fall in one straight fore-and-aft line.

archetype.basis:
A dogleg archetype now exists and this car matches none, for a reason worth stating precisely. Its construction is unestablished, which alone would leave it deviating on a gap. What excludes it is the downshift blip, recorded as required - a known value, not a gap - where the archetype has it optional because a synchromesh does not need one to engage.

That is the dataset's own rule: required is reserved for gearboxes that need the blip. So this record asserts, through the blip, a construction its gearbox_type does not establish. Ten records are in that position and it predates this classification; the note records it as a question rather than resolving it here. Establishing the construction settles both fields at once.
